sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Anil Kumar,Prabhat Kumar Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Nirbhay Singh Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging the commission of an offence under Section 376 IPC,
initially, the FIR in question was lodged as a missing person report.
3. Counsel for the applicant has filed supplementary affidavit, wherein, the victim has turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution story.
4. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the said subsequent development couple with the fact that applicant has no criminal history, applicant is in custody since 07.07.2022 and there being nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Sharafat be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 341 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC & 3/4 POCSO Act, P.S. Kasganj, District Kasganj, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs. 25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 17.8.2023 S.A.
